correctness.rationale: The state-dependent birth and death rates follow exactly from the two independent site samplings. The backward equations yield the product formula. For all integers K>=3, L>=2K-3, derivative of log[gamma(L-1)^2/((i-1)(L-i))] is nonnegative for each i=2..K-1 and strictly positive at larger L, proving all-capacity cutoff; no numerical-only extrapolation. Explicit exact rational coefficients for K=4,5 show D_5,7 > D_5,5 and give D_5,6-D_5,5=gamma(44+226gamma-253gamma^2)/48. The quadratic has exactly one positive root. The checker executes independent exact backward-equation solves and coefficient comparisons.

The classical birth-death backward recurrence is explicitly acknowledged as prior theory. Closest papers address different population mechanisms or objectives. A nontrivial unlocated prior implication remains possible and independent audit is not performed.

value.rationale: Habitat reduction in small sexually reproducing populations is a documented conservation-design mechanism. Requiring two founders to reach a prespecified recovery target is a natural finite-risk measure distinct from indefinite survival. The first nontrivial target, exact capacity switch, and universal finite search interval characterize when additional habitat space outweighs dilution of mate encounters. This supplies an interpretable structural boundary and reproducible ecological benchmark, not an arbitrary slice or tiny parameter gain.
